why: Overlay milestone, step 1. Without it disks can only be changed by editing autorun.txt on the card. Pure logic with a host test, no rendering or timing risk, and the catalogue everything else lists.
Overlay milestone, step 2: four drives and runtime mount/eject, the actual feature the user asked for. The FDC already decodes drives 0-3, so this is plumbing.
Overlay milestone, step 3: F12, key capture that cannot leak into BASIC, pause with the HDMI audio held at digital silence. The riskiest slice, so its logic gets a host test first.
Overlay milestone, step 4: the look. Cheap now: g_card and coco_boot_card_present already draw 6847 text over the machine; it needs an inverse attribute and the list layout.
Built and committed, awaiting a hardware check: RUN cold-starts to BASIC without AUTORUN. Minutes to verify on a spare board.
The BOOT button as a second way into the overlay. Its first step is a spike (read BOOTSEL without disturbing DVI and audio) that can run any time on a spare board; step 2 needs 81c.

The 2026-09-17 soak log stops at about 17 h (docs/measurements/logs/2026-09-17-1951-pizero_stream_60.log); the ticket still needs a full 25 h run. With four boards it no longer blocks development: soak one while working on another.

First of the BUILT-BUT-UNSEEN batch: boot pages, the GIME timer, the palette, the case. All are written and host-tested and none has met hardware. Do them in ONE session when the soak ends rather than four visits. This one is quickest to check: rename bas12.rom on the card and power on.
Same session: flash pizero_gime and run a CoCo 3 timer program. Also the only way to settle the reload-quirk revision, which sets the tempo of anything written against it.

Same session, needs the keyboard: play something audible. Two things changed under it (in-spec 60 Hz timing, and the 0.9% shortfall gone), and it is the only way to hear whether PIZERO-121's 8.7 discarded samples a second matter.

Also built and unseen: the audio rate servo. Verified only by simulating the loop for six hours of model time, so the NEXT soak is its real test. Flash it with the same session, then start soak #2 and watch fill hold near 4,400 with skips flat.

Still the worst daily-use defect: a keyboard attached after boot never enumerates, which cost us a power cycle mid-measurement today. No longer a freeze suspect, since the soak is clean, so it is a usability fix rather than a stability one.

Demoted from 3 to 9: the mechanism is understood (our symbol stream is legal but the hardest case for a receiver's equalisation, and this monitor fails on colour in one region) and no other sink has shown it. Pair with PIZERO-99; re-raise immediately if a second screen shows it.
Other people's screens, which the kit rests on, and the same session answers whether the fuzz follows the board or the monitor.
Turns vetting into something every build repeats. The harness and 74 host tests exist now, so this is mostly assembly: a firmware build that runs the checks and prints PASS with the measured number.
Decide before building the launch path: cold boot, hot swap, or both on different keys. Fruit Jam is inconsistent with itself here, which is the evidence that leaving it implicit does not work.
Selecting something finally starts it. Blocked on porting coco_machine_reset() and on the PIZERO-115 decision.
The palette editor and per-title .pal profiles, which need the overlay. The register file underneath them is already done, so this is UI work rather than machine work.
CoCo 3 track, stage 1: a 6809 lockstep correctness harness. Host only, and the precondition for touching the core at all.
CoCo 3 track, stage 2: the 1.79 MHz benchmark and baseline, so the speed work has a target.
CoCo 3 track, stage 3: the speed-up the whole CoCo 3 effort hangs on. Its gate decides whether PIZERO-133 happens.
CoCo 3 track, stage 4, behind the PIZERO-131 gate and the PIZERO-135 decisions.
